text:
maya: Heads up — after pushing AWQ-v2 to ded-cluster-3 we're seeing sporadic OOMs on 8xA100 nodes during long-context chat sessions. Symptoms: steady KV cache growth + allocator fragmentation spikes. Sharing quick profile below.

sam: Can you paste the heap timeline and kernel switch counts? Are we hitting kernel fallbacks mid-request?

maya: Paste from perf-trace (trimmed):
```
time    kv_cache_bytes   allocator_free_frag   kernel_switches
00:00   1.2G             120MB                 4
00:10   2.1G             560MB                 38  # steady growth
00:20   2.6G             1.1GB                124 
00:30   2.9G             980MB                 142 (oom)
```
Also saw many fallbacks listed as `awq_conv -> fallback_gemm` in kernel logs.

liam: That timeline screams mixed-precision upcasting. We changed the dispatch path to upcast some AWQ tensors to fp32 for a subset of kernels — that effectively doubles the KV cache footprint when copies are materialized. Did the rollout flip `kv_upcast_on_insert`?

maya: Yes — the change was meant to stabilize kernels with small kernels that had numeric issues. Rolling it enabled auto-upcast on insert+dispatch. It reduces rare numeric repros but blows up memory in steady-state.

eva: Related: batching heuristics may be amplifying this. When we accumulate large batch windows the kernel selector prefers dense GEMM kernels which allocate large transient workspaces. Combined with upcast temporaries you get double+ workspace. Could tighten the batching window or prefer streaming kernels for long-context chat routes.

raj: Suggested short mitigations to try in canary: 
- Flip `kv_dtype_persist=true` so the KV cache preserves AWQ int8 layout and only casts on-kernel-dispatch.
- Lower `batch_hint_ms` from 8 -> 4 for chat route to reduce contiguous group sizes.
- Tweak allocator: set `min_slab_compact_bytes=16777216` (16MB) and enable `aggressive_coalesce=true` to reduce fragmentation.

maya: Quick repro patch I ran locally:
```bash
# toggle runtime flags via admin API
curl -X POST https://console/api/runtime/config \
  -d '{"kv_dtype_persist": true, "batch_hint_ms": 4, "allocator": {"min_slab_compact_bytes": 16777216, "aggressive_coalesce": true}}'
```
Local run looked promising — KV growth flattened and allocator free-frag dropped ~60%. Need non-prod canary on ded-cluster-3.

infra-bot: [ALERT] deployment AWQ-v2 rolled to ded-cluster-3 at 2026-03-16T22:11:05Z. 12 OOM alerts in the last 24h. Ticket: #INF-4921.

sam: Also capture kernel-selector debug logs. We're seeing ~124 kernel_switches -> fallback_gemm as you pasted. That fallback path currently allocates fp32 temporaries of size ~0.5-1.2x of working set. If we can add an fp16 fallback kernel or a quant-aware fallback it would help.

liam: Short term: prefer keeping quantized KV memory layout persistent. Long term: add quant-aware fallback kernels and avoid host/device roundtrip of casts. We should also add a small on-device compaction pass that runs when GPU is idle for >200ms to coalesce free slices.

maya: Plan of action: 
1) Roll `kv_dtype_persist=true` to 5% canary for chat routes.
2) Deploy allocator params change cluster-wide as experiment.
3) Reduce batch_hint for the affected route.
4) Instrument more detailed kernel memory trace (per-kernel temp bytes) and add regression alert if resident rises >15% vs baseline.

raj: I'll open a PR with the flag toggles + allocator defaults and add a small smoke test to the perf harness.

maya: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3245 (canary flags + allocator knobs). Monitoring dashboards pinned.

sam: sgtm. After canary, if OOMs persist we'll try an on-the-fly compaction and schedule a follow-up to implement quant-aware fallbacks.

eva: Also add a perf unit test that simulates long sequences with AWQ models and asserts no >20% growth in KV bytes over 30s.

liam: FYI I ran a microbenchmark: with kv_dtype_persist=false we hit 2.8GB KV vs 1.4GB when true (same request mix). Will attach logs to the PR.

maya: Thanks — will monitor canary and collect traces. If we see immediate improvement we'll keep the persist flag and prioritize long-term kernel work.

raj: I'll coordinate canary rollout and tag ops for increased alerting sensitivity.

sam: :thumbsup:

liam: happy to pair on kernel fallback PR once we have stable reproducer.

maya: tagging folks: @sam @liam @eva @raj. Will update thread with canary results.
